title: Interactive Gambling Amendment (Sports Betting Reform) Bill 2015
short_title: Interactive Gambling Amendment (Sports Betting Reform) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would add harm-reduction rules for online sports betting to the Interactive Gambling Act 2001.
It would create a new regulator to monitor compliance and set up a national register for people who want to exclude themselves from online sports betting.
The new rules would take effect three months after the bill becomes law.
changes: Creates a new definition of 'restricted wagering services' for websites that accept bets on sports and races.
Establishes an Interactive Gambling Regulator to enforce the new obligations.
Sets up a National Self-exclusion Register for online sports betting.
Introduces a 'betting limit' that lets individuals set a maximum amount of their own money they can bet over a period.
Defines when a restricted wagering service is considered to have provided credit or verified a customer's identity.
summary.affected: Online sports betting providers and individuals who use them.
